How will private deployments show in the same console?
What's the expected latency impact of prefix caching?
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-25 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Ellen Wu (Redwood SE), Alex Rivera (Shoreline Head of MLOps), Priya Kapoor (Platform Lead), Tom Nguyen (FinOps), Sara B. (Security)

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. this is Maya from Redwood, i manage the account — i'll hand over to Ravi and Ellen to show the console and route-cost stuff.
[00:12] Alex Rivera: Thanks, Maya. real quick — high level, we run most user-facing models in a hosted environment but have a couple private stacks for PHI flows. FinOps wants per-feature chargeback, so we wanna see route-level costs.
[00:25] Ravi Patel: perfect — that's exactly what the console was built for. we'll pull up the usage lens, and then show how you can split by route, tag, and service. quick question: what's your rough qps for those private routes?
[00:39] Priya Kapoor: Private routes are small right now, like 8–12 qps each, but peak bursts up to ~120 qps for the clinical triage flow.
[00:47] Ellen Wu: cool, that helps. and the hosted traffic?
[00:50] Alex Rivera: hosted is heavier — about 1.2k qps across 4 public routes.
[00:55] Maya Chen: ok noted. goal for today: walkthrough per-route dashboards, show token-level cost breakdown, then map to chargeback examples.

[01:20] Ravi Patel: (screen) so this is the console Home. first card is the Usage Heatmap — you can filter timeframe, region, and model family. if you click into Routes, you get a per-route list with tokens, avg latency, tail p95, and cost attribution.
[01:40] Tom Nguyen: when you say cost attribution — is that inference-only, or does it include infra e.g., GPU amortization?
[01:48] Ravi Patel: good call — by default it's inference cost (tokens * model unit cost + runtime overhead). we can add custom overhead lines for infra amortization or reserved GPU commitments. people usually add a fixed per-hour infra cost and let the console apportion it by consumed tokens or by time-in-use.
[02:10] Tom Nguyen: so i could add our reserved capacity monthly commit and then have the console split it across routes?
[02:13] Ravi Patel: yep, exactly — you can upload your reserved capacity sku and the console will pro-rate it based on route usage.

[02:40] Ellen Wu: quick demo — i'm going to open the Route Cost Breakdown for 'clinical-triage'. note the subtlety: we show prompt vs completion tokens, model variant chosen, and a rolling quantization multiplier if you're using smaller variants.
[02:58] Priya Kapoor: rollover question — we use an open model quantized to 4-bit on private infra; will Redwood show cost parity between hosted quantized variants and private 4-bit runtime?
[03:09] Ravi Patel: yes, we surface model variant cost and a per-token runtime multiplier. the UI label might be misleading in the transcription — sometimes it shows as 'Red bud runtime' in auto captions — but it's the Redwood runtime multiplier. for private deployments we ingest your on-prem cost profile and show an apples-to-apples comparison.

[03:40] Alex Rivera: and latency: if we add prefix caching or KV cache on private stack, will the latency numbers in the console reflect that improvement?
[03:48] Ellen Wu: mmhmm — caching effects show up in the per-route latency histograms; we also show cache hit-rate as a separate metric and estimate token savings from cache. there was a small delay in metrics collection earlier today but the numbers line up after a 10–15 minute rollup.

[04:20] Tom Nguyen: pricing model nuance — do you support multiple pricing models per customer, e.g., hosted per-token + private per-hour?
[04:28] Ravi Patel: yes, the console supports mixed SKUs. you can assign routes to billing buckets — for example 'hosted-per-token' for public routes, and 'reserved-capacity' for private ones. the cost engine normalizes to a per-token equivalent but keeps the original sku for billing exports.

[05:05] Maya Chen: can we jump to a chargeback example? Ravi — walk us through mapping route -> product sku -> cost center.
[05:12] Ravi Patel: sure. (navigates) here's a sample mapping we set up for another health customer: routes tagged with product codes (triage, notes, summarization) map to cost centers. you can export the allocation CSV and plug into your internal chargeback system — or use our direct billing export if you want to ingest into your billing pipeline.
[05:40] Priya Kapoor: are tags and mapping automated? we have dynamic routes created by the app team.
[05:46] Ellen Wu: tags can be auto-injected at request time via a header or SDK param; if you can't change the client we also support a routing table where patterns are matched to routes.

[06:10] Alex Rivera: security: Sara — any quick questions on SSO and KMS?
[06:15] Sara B.: yes — we need SSO via SAML, SCIM provisioning, and KMS-based CMEK for logs and model artifacts. also audit logs retention for 2 years.
[06:25] Ravi Patel: we have enterprise integrations: SAML SSO + SCIM, RBAC roles in console, and KMS integrations with major cloud vendors. audit logs can be exported to your S3 or syslog with configurable retention. note: for Private deployments we can enable local HSM/KMS via connectors.
[06:45] Priya Kapoor: does enabling CMEK change runtime performance?
[06:48] Ellen Wu: negligible for inference path; there is a small overhead on key retrieval for initial model load, though we cache key material.

[07:10] Tom Nguyen: back to cost — can the console break out prompt vs completion cost across routes over the last 30 days?
[07:16] Ravi Patel: yep — filter timeframe 30d, group by route, and the cost waterfall shows prompt/completion/runtime/overhead. we can toggle currency and you can provide internal exchange rates if you run multi-region.

[08:00] (screen) Ravi Patel: showing the 'Cost Waterfall' now. note at the top there's a slider to switch between modeled cost and actual billed cost (if you link billing exports). modeled is useful for forecasting.
[08:18] Alex Rivera: can we run alerts on anomalies for a route — like sudden cost spike?
[08:22] Ellen Wu: yes — set alert rule: route 'summarizer' cost > 30% daily increase and notify slack/email and create a ticket in your tracker. we also have automated anomaly detection you can opt into — it runs weekly scans and surfaces suspicious regressions.

[09:00] Priya Kapoor: one practical thing — do you support exporting the route mapping to our accounting system? our finance team uses a specific csv template.
[09:06] Ravi Patel: we support customizable export templates; you can map columns and we can add a header row matching your import.

[09:30] (interruption) Alex Rivera: sorry — just want to confirm private stack visibility. will the same console show per-route metrics for both hosted and private?
[09:38] Maya Chen: yes, the console aggregates across deployment modes when you opt in. for private, we ship a metrics agent that pushes telemetry to your private control plane, which then mirrors selected metrics into Redwood console with privacy controls. it's not shipping raw logs out by default.

[10:10] Sara B.: is the telemetry encrypted in transit?
[10:12] Ravi Patel: yes, TLS 1.2+ and mutual TLS for the agent connection. we also support customer-managed keys for telemetry at rest.

[11:00] Tom Nguyen: i'm interested in an example showing the financial impact of batching and quantization across a high-volume route. can you show a before/after?
[11:08] Ellen Wu: sure. (uses demo dataset) route 'search-assist' — baseline hosted gpt-like variant costs X, with batching + dynamic quantization it drops to ~0.49X. here the console shows estimated monthly savings column and the break-even time for reserved vs pay-as-you-go.
[11:40] Priya Kapoor: these are modeled estimates — how do we validate them in a pilot?
[11:44] Ravi Patel: we usually run a 1-week pilot with a representative workload: you provide routes and a replay or synthetic load, we run the pilot against both hosted and private variants and deliver a benchmark report with real p50/p95 and token cost. guide and checklist attached after call.

[12:10] Alex Rivera: what about model rollouts — can you do canary splits by route and automatically fallback to cheaper model if quality metrics pass?
[12:19] Ellen Wu: yep — console supports canary deploys and automatic fallback policies. you can define quality checks via our eval hooks or plug in a custom metric; if quality drops we failover to the previous model.

[13:00] Maya Chen: (recap) so action items: we'll send pricing and the pilot checklist; you (Priya) to share route list and qps; schedule pilot kickoff.

[13:20] Alex Rivera: quick procurement question — what's the lead time for Dedicated pools?
[13:25] Ravi Patel: depends on capacity and region but typically 3–6 weeks for provision. for private on-prem it's variable; we do a discovery and provide a rollout plan.

[14:00] Tom Nguyen: on compliance — do you have SOC 2? and what's your ISO stance?
[14:05] Maya Chen: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II; we also have ISO 27001 in progress and provide security package with pen test reports, encryption details, and our shared responsibility model.

[14:40] (customer clarifies finance flows)
[15:00] Priya Kapoor: one more — can per-route tags be derived from API keys? we issue service-bound API keys per feature.
[15:07] Ellen Wu: yes, we can map API key to a route at ingestion and apply the tag automatically. that works well for chargeback when keys are already service-scoped.

[15:30] Alex Rivera: any known gotchas with streaming responses and cost attribution? we use streaming for low-latency UI.
[15:36] Ravi Patel: streaming is attributed by tokens produced; we track both in-flight and final token counts. for partial streams we estimate costs conservatively until completion. some early transcripts can show odd numbers but final reconciliation uses the completed token count.

[16:10] (wrap-up) Maya Chen: ok that covers the console demo. quick open items: security package link, pilot pricing, benchmark checklist. we'll send those in an email and schedule kickoff.
[16:27] Alex Rivera: thanks — this was helpful. expecting the pilot docs.
[16:32] Tom Nguyen: i'll review with finance and put in a tentative PO timeline.
[16:35] Priya Kapoor: i'll compile the route list and qps and share before EOD 8/30.
[16:41] Maya Chen: great — thanks everyone.

Notes on transcription: auto-caption occasionally mislabels 'Redwood runtime' as 'Red bud runtime' and 'KV cache' came out as 'K-V cash' in a few spots; some speaker labels conflated 'Ellen' and 'Ravi' at the start of the demo; timestamps approximate.

End of transcript.
